answer: In PoA, each bonded identity is an escrowed vertex, so coordinated equivocation by k identities triggers aggregate penalties proportional to k², rather than k independent fines. Detection also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the sybil controller through correlated slashing and asymmetric depreciation, making large swarms economically untenable. The walnut-and-velvet distinction is irrelevant: bonded stake, evidence, and correlation determine recovery.
